title: Per-tenant flow-control multiplexer for console metrics stream
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
We currently apply coarse-grained throttling at the ingress gateway and a global queue limiter in the metrics ingest cluster. This causes noisy neighbors during bursts: a single heavy customer can push global queues into backpressure and increase tail latency for everyone.

Goal:
Implement a per-tenant flow-control multiplexer in the real-time console metrics pipeline that: (1) enforces soft/hard per-tenant throughput limits, (2) exposes backpressure signals upstream to the gateway and SDKs, (3) allows dynamic limit updates from quota service, and (4) falls back to a global limiter for unregistered or anonymous traffic.

Scope and constraints:
- This work focuses on pipeline components inside the metrics ingress cluster (stream processors and ingress gateway interface). We will not change storage tiers in this ticket.
- Memory footprint per-tenant must remain bounded: expect ~15k active tenants in peak region, average token metadata ~120 bytes => design must cap memory and evict cold tenants.
- Integration points: dynamic quota service (read-only API), ingress gRPC for backpressure, console-observability telemetry for per-tenant SLOs.

Non-goals:
- Billing/chargeback integration (handled in separate PM ticket).
- Long-term historical reprocessing/retention changes.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant token-bucket applied to streaming ingress with configurable soft and hard limits per tenant
Upstream gateway receives and reacts to backpressure signal via existing gRPC control channel within 250ms of sustained exceedance
System falls back to existing global limiter when tenant metadata is missing or tenant flagged as 'unmanaged'
Memory usage for tenant controller stays under 1.2GB at 15k active tenants in load test
End-to-end latency P95 for tenant-scoped requests does not regress more than 10% vs baseline for normal traffic patterns
Automated integration tests cover dynamic limit updates and eviction behavior
Runtime metrics (per-tenant QPS, tokens_used, evictions) are emitted and visible on console-telemetry dashboard
tasks: Design: define token-bucket parameters, eviction policy, and shard key strategy (owner: Maya)
Prototype: implement in-stream processor operator that maintains per-tenant buckets (owner: Luca)
Gateway adaptation: wire gRPC backpressure control messages and test end-to-end (owner: Priya)
Quota integration: read-only periodic sync with quota service with caching and TTL (owner: Luca)
Load testing: k6/bench harness for 15k tenant simulation and memory profiling (owner: SRE team)
Observability: add per-tenant metrics and dashboards, alerting on eviction rate and sustained backpressure (owner: Observability)
Canary rollout: feature flag, 5% of traffic then 25% then 100% with rollback playbook (owner: Ops)
Documentation: design doc and runbook for failures and fallback (owner: Maya)
Security review: surface for review if any tenant metadata includes PII (owner: Security)
Create integration tests and CI gating PRs (owner: Luca)
load_test_results: 2025-03-01: synthetic run with 12k tenants: memory 980MB, P95 latency +6%
2025-03-04: burst test with 16k tenants: observed eviction rate 3.2% caused by TTL-based eviction; tuning required
rollout_plan: Toggle feature-flag in ingest config: off -> canary(5%) -> ramp(25%) -> full(100%)
During canary: monitor evictions, per-tenant P95, and gateway backpressure metrics every 5m
Abort criteria: eviction rate > 5% sustained for 10 minutes OR P95 regressions > 20% for non-canary tenants
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: per-tenant state explosion from bursty onboarding of new tenants. Mitigation: strong LRU eviction with cooldown and sample-based telemetry to identify abusive clients.

Risk: upstream gateways may introduce head-of-line blocking when many tenants signal backpressure. Mitigation: gateway will multiplex signals and enforce per-route exponential backoff rather than blocking worker threads.
Risk: stale quota info leading to incorrect throttling. Mitigation: implement TTL-based cache with async refresh and a 'grace' mode that uses previous quota for 30s while fetching.
Risk: observability cardinality explosion. Mitigation: only emit detailed per-tenant metrics for flagged tenants and aggregate others by bucketed tiers (S0/S1/S2).
